_comment: Public RSS/Atom feeds. All free, all keyless, all fetched with a normal
browser user agent and cached for 30 minutes so we stay a polite client.
trust_url_kind: whether the site's URL path reliably states the deal type.
Travelzoo files each deal under /cruises/, /hotels/, /vacations/ and so
on, so its URL is the single best signal available. Fly4Free files
everything under /flight-deals/ including its hotel and package posts,
so trusting its URL mislabels a third of that feed as flights.
Sources set to enabled:false were measured and left off - see 'why'.
affiliate: optional. An outbound-link template with {url} where the
Leave it out and links are untouched. This is the hook for making the
report earn something once you have traffic; a broken tracker silently
killing every link would cost more than it earns, so it is opt-in.

sources.name: theflightdeal
sources.note: Most structured feed of the lot: 'Airline: Origin - Dest. $NNN. Roundtrip'. US origins.

sources.name: fly4free
sources.note: Flights, hotels and packages, European origins, EUR/GBP pricing. High volume.

sources.name: travelzoo
sources.note: The only reliable source of cruise and package deals here. ~265 items per pull.

sources.name: reddit-flightdeals
sources.note: Atom. Heavy on European business-class fares. Rate limits if hit often - the 30 min cache matters.

sources.name: reddit-awardtravel
sources.note: Award availability and transfer bonuses. Mostly cash-free so few rows survive parsing.

sources.name: reddit-traveldeals
sources.why: Verified and rejected. Despite the name it is a coupon and gift-card resale sub (Ixigo, MakeMyTrip, referral codes), not a deal feed. Measured 1 parseable item in 25, and that one was a private hotel-booking resale. Added no US flight coverage, which was the reason for trying it.

sources.name: cruisefever
sources.why: Measured 1 priced item in 20. It is a cruise news site, not a deal feed.

sources.name: cruisehive
sources.why: Measured 0 priced items in 9. News only.

sources.name: secretflying
sources.why: Cloudflare serves an HTML challenge page instead of the feed. Nothing to parse.
